original_value: Video-based moving vehicle detection and tracking is an important prerequisite for vehicle counting under complex transportation environments. However, in the complex natural scene, the conventional optical flow method cannot accurately detect the boundary of the moving vehicle due to the generation of the shadow. In addition, traditional vehicle tracking algorithms are often occluded by trees, buildings, etc., and particle filters are also susceptible to particle degradation. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a kind of moving vehicle detection and tracking based on the optical flow method and immune particle filter algorithm. The proposed method firstly uses the optical flow method to roughly detect the moving vehicle and then uses the shadow detection algorithm based on the HSV color space to mark the shadow position after threshold segmentation and further combines the region-labeling algorithm to realize the shadow removal and accurately detect the moving vehicle. Improved affinity calculation and mutation function of antibody are proposed to make the particle filter algorithm have certain adaptivity and robustness to scene interference. Experiments are carried out in complex traffic scenes with shadow and occlusion interference. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can well solve the interference of shadow and occlusion and realize accurate detection and robust tracking of moving vehicles under complex transportation environments, which has the potentiality to be processed on a cloud computing platform.

result.paraphrase: Video-based moving vehicle detection and tracking is an essential prerequisite for vehicle counting in complex traffic environments. In complex natural scenes, however, conventional optical flow methods cannot accurately identify moving-vehicle boundaries because of shadow generation. Moreover, traditional vehicle tracking algorithms are often obstructed by trees, buildings, and similar objects, and particle filters are also prone to particle degradation. To address this, this paper proposes a moving vehicle detection and tracking approach based on an optical flow method and an immune particle filter algorithm. The proposed method first uses optical flow to roughly detect moving vehicles, then applies an HSV color-space-based shadow detection algorithm to mark shadow locations after threshold segmentation, and further combines a region-labeling algorithm to remove shadows and accurately detect moving vehicles. Improved affinity calculation and an antibody mutation function are introduced to give the particle filter algorithm adaptability and robustness against scene interference. Experiments are conducted in complex traffic scenes with shadow and occlusion interference. The results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively handle shadow and occlusion interference and achieve accurate detection and robust tracking of moving vehicles in complex transportation environments, with potential for implementation on a cloud computing platform.
